Later, he extended his leadership to the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI), holding positions such as State Secretary and All-India Joint Secretary. His political career began through the Students' Federation of India (SFI), and he previously served as the General Secretary of the Calicut University Union. After serving as a member of the Kannur District Panchayat, he was elected twice to the Lok Sabha from the Kannur constituency. Later, he joined the Indian National Congress and was elected twice to the Kerala Legislative Assembly, representing the Kannur constituency. He also contested as the BJP candidate in the bye-election for the Malappuram Lok Sabha constituency.

b: Abhayakumar Nalukettil is an award-winning architect, academician, and the recipient of the 2024 National HUDCO Design Award. His multidisciplinary work explores the vital relationship between the built environment,…
f: Abhayakumar Nalukettil is an award-winning architect, academician, and the recipient of the 2024 National HUDCO Design Award. His multidisciplinary work explores the vital relationship between the built environment, urban culture, and community well-being. As the founder of the Trivandrum Runners Club (TRaCs), he pioneered organized long-distance running in Kerala’s capital. Under his leadership, the club introduced the city’s first full marathon in 2014 and launched unique events like the Women’s Midnight Run. In 2018, he collaborated with the Kerala government to organize a marathon for the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund following the state's floods. An accomplished athlete himself, Abhay has competed in major events including the Mumbai Marathon. He is also one of the few AIMS-trained Marathon Race Course Measurers in India, ensuring international standards for professional races. Furthering his sports engagement, he is a Director and Co-owner of Kombans FC, Thiruvananthapuram’s first professional football club. Through his diverse career, he advocates for inclusive, active, and people-centric urban environments. Today, he continues to bridge the gap between architectural design, professional sport, and civic life.

f: Abhirami Ajai is a talented musician and playback singer who rose to fame with the popular song "Thottu Thottu" from the movie Diamond Necklace. She entered the playback singing industry at a very young age, recording that hit track when she was just thirteen. Throughout her career, she has collaborated with legendary composers such as Vidyasagar, Ouseppachan, and Gopi Sunder. Some of her most notable hits include "Azhalinte Azhangalil" from Ayalum Njanum Thammil, "Omanakomala" from Oru Indian Pranayakadha, "Madhumathippoo" from Geethaanjali, and "Poovithalay" from Thoppil Joppan. A dedicated student of music, she was trained under the guidance of Perumbavoor G. Raveendranath, Dr. Lakshmi Menon, and Dr. K.N. Ranganatha Sharma. Beyond her film career, she has performed in numerous classical music concerts and has had the honor of performing Sangeetharchana at Puttaparthi on three occasions. In addition to her musical talents, she is also a writer of English poetry.

f: Abida Rasheed is a celebrated culinary expert and entrepreneur from Kozhikode, famously known as the Queen of Mappila Cuisine. After a long career in the textile industry, she dedicated herself to preserving and promoting the unique flavors of the Malabar Muslim community, which are rooted in centuries of Arab-Malayali trade history. By championing traditional techniques like slow-cooking and manual grinding, she has moved from her grandmother’s kitchen to the world stage, consulting for luxury hotels and hosting global food festivals. Today, she serves as a vital cultural guardian, sharing the heritage of Malabar through her signature dishes, culinary tours, and documentation of heirloom recipes.

Irish-born, he has reported across Africa, the Middle East and South Asia, covering major conflicts and political upheavals. Formerly The Guardian’s Pakistan–Afghanistan correspondent, his investigations — including the Axact degree fraud exposé — ultimately led to his expulsion from Pakistan in 2013. He is the author of The Nine Lives of Pakistan and a recipient of multiple honours, including the George Polk Award and the James Foley Medill Medal for Courage, and lives in Nairobi with his wife and twin sons.

Founder of the Bhasha Research Centre and the Adivasi Academy, he also led the landmark People’s Linguistic Survey of India. He is currently Senior Professor of Eminence and Director at Somaiya Vidyavihar University and a recipient of the Padmashri and several international honours.

Jayaram began his journey in the world of performing arts through mimicry and played a pivotal role in popularizing the art form through the renowned troupe Kalabhavan. He made his cinematic debut in Padmarajan’s masterpiece Aparan. Some of his most notable performances can be seen in films such as Sesham, Theerthadanam, Moonnam Pakkam, Sandesham, Meleparambil Aanveedu, Thooval Kottaram, Ozler, Thenali, and the epic Ponniyin Selvan. He is married to the acclaimed actress Parvathy, and they have two children: Malavika and the actor Kalidas Jayaram.

His filmography includes other notable works such as Mr. & Ms. Rowdy, Argentina Fans Kaattoorkadavu, and Happy Sardar. In addition to his lead role in the Tamil film Oru Pakka Kathai, he has delivered standout performances in major productions like Vikram and Raayan. He is married to Tarini Kalingarayar, who was the third runner-up in the Miss Diva beauty pageant.

f: Makarand R. Paranjape is Sri Aurobindo Chair (Hon.) at Vedere University and Director of Education at Access Health Care Physicians, Florida. He served as Professor of English at Jawaharlal Nehru University for nearly 25 years and was Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, Shimla (2018–2021). A poet, novelist, critic, and commentator, he has authored/edited 55 books and published over 200 academic papers. His ongoing columns include “Soft Power” (Open), “Right in the Middle” (The New Indian Express), and “US Sutra” (FirstPost). His recent works include Hindutva and Hind Swaraj (2025), Mahatma Gandhi: Mrityu aur Punarutthan (2024), Identity’s Last Secret (2023), JNU: Nationalism and India's Uncivil War (2022), and Swami Vivekananda: Hinduism and India’s Road to Modernity (2020).

b: Manu S. Pillai is a historian and the author of five books, most recently Gods, Guns & Missionaries: The Making of the Modern Hindu Identity. He won the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar for his debut book, The Ivory…
f: Manu S. Pillai is a historian and the author of five books, most recently Gods, Guns & Missionaries: The Making of the Modern Hindu Identity. He won the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar for his debut book, The Ivory Throne, and writes as a columnist for Mint Lounge. Born in Kerala in 1990, he was educated at Fergusson College, Pune, and King’s College London, where he earned a PhD in history. His academic work includes research on nineteenth-century religious nationalism. Manu has also worked in parliamentary offices in New Delhi and London and was commissioned by the BBC as a researcher on the Incarnations history series.

b: Martin Goodman is the author of 14 books spanning prize-winning nonfiction and fiction, including My Head for a Tree and Client Earth, the latter named Judges’ Choice at the UK Business Book of the Year Awards and Green…
f: Martin Goodman is the author of 14 books spanning prize-winning nonfiction and fiction, including My Head for a Tree and Client Earth, the latter named Judges’ Choice at the UK Business Book of the Year Awards and Green Book of the Year by Santa Monica Libraries. His biography of J S Haldane, Suffer & Survive, won Best Book (Basis of Medicine) from the British Medical Association, while his debut novel On Bended Knees was shortlisted for the Whitbread Prize. Goodman’s work frequently engages with India, from spiritual biography to environmental writing, and he also authored I Was Carlos Castaneda, praised by the Los Angeles Times for its bold exploration of Peruvian shamanism. He has taught across Europe, Asia and the Middle East, and his experiences have inspired novels such as The Cellist of Dachau and his eco-cyber thriller The Boy on the Train. An emeritus professor of Creative Writing at the University of Hull and former director of the Philip Larkin Centre, Goodman has also created radio documentaries for the BBC and continues to pursue interests including piano and bird habitats

b: Mohammad Azharuddin is widely regarded as one of India's greatest cricketers and a former captain of the national team. A native of Hyderabad, he transitioned into a significant political career as a Congress leader and…
f: Mohammad Azharuddin is widely regarded as one of India's greatest cricketers and a former captain of the national team. A native of Hyderabad, he transitioned into a significant political career as a Congress leader and currently serves as a minister in the Telangana government, holding the portfolio for Minority Affairs. During his illustrious sporting career, he represented India in 99 Test matches and 334 One Day Internationals (ODIs). He amassed over 6,000 runs in Tests and more than 9,000 runs in ODIs, scoring 22 Test centuries and 7 ODI centuries. In 1989, he succeeded K. Srikkanth as the captain of the Indian team, eventually leading the side in 47 Tests and 174 ODIs. Under his leadership, India participated in an ODI World Cup and secured an Asia Cup title. After retiring from professional cricket, he became active in politics and was elected to the Lok Sabha from the Moradabad constituency. He later served as the President of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee. In recognition of his sporting achievements, the nation honored him with the Arjuna Award, and he was also named a Wisden Cricketer of the Year. His life was the subject of the Bollywood biographical film titled Azhar.

f: P.V. Shajikumar is a prominent Malayalam short story writer, Novelist and screenwriter who has made significant contributions to literature and cinema. His celebrated short story collections include ‘Janam’, ‘Vellarippadam’, ‘Kidappasamaram’, ‘Ullal’, ‘G.L.P. Uzal Keekankot’, ‘Katha’, and ‘Sthalam’. Shajikumar has also penned memoirs such as ‘Kaalichampothilekku Oru Half-Ticket’, ‘Itha Innumuthal; Itha Innale Vare’, and ‘Kadhayum Pathraangalum Saankalpikam Alla’. His debut novel ‘Maranavamsham’ is another notable work that solidifies his literary prowess. In cinema, Shajikumar has gained recognition for his screenplays for films like ‘Kanyaka Talkies’, ‘Take Off’, and ‘Teacher’, while also scripting the dialogues for ‘Puthan Panam’. His accolades include prestigious honors such as the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar, New York Film Festival Award for Best Screenplay, Shanghai Film Festival Award for Best Screenplay, and the Vayalar Award. Additionally, he has been recognized with the Kerala Government Youth Icon Award, Swami Vivekananda Yuva Pratibha Award, and several literary awards, including the Kerala Sahitya Akademi-Geetha Hiranyan Endowment, C.V. Sriraman Award, and Kunjunni Mash Award.

f: Film professional, actor, and advertising film director. He made his acting debut as the notable villain DySP George in the film Thudarum. Among his most notable works are the “Pug” commercial for Hutch and the “Zoozoo” commercials for Airtel. He has also made advertising films for Michael Bay. He produced the film Ezhu Sundara Rathrikal.

f: Shabana Azmi is one of the most respected and influential actors in Indian cinema. Her debut performance in Ankur was widely praised, with filmmaker Satyajit Ray describing her as the finest dramatic actress of the country. The film marked the beginning of an extraordinary career. Over five decades, she has acted in more than 140 Hindi films and 12 international productions. She has worked with leading filmmakers from India and abroad, including Deepa Mehta, Mira Nair, Gurinder Chadha, Ismail Merchant, Shekhar Kapur, and Steven Spielberg. Her work spans meaningful cinema as well as mainstream films, reflecting her range and longevity. Shabana Azmi is the only Indian actress to win five National Film Awards for Best Actress, including three in consecutive years. She has also won six Filmfare Awards and numerous international honours. She has received every major acting award in India, many of them multiple times. Her contribution to theatre is equally significant. She has delivered acclaimed performances in landmark plays such as Tumhari Amrita, one of the longest-running plays in Indian theatre, along with Broken Images, Kaifi Aur Main, and productions staged in London and Singapore. Beyond the arts, Azmi is a committed social activist. She believes strongly in the power of art to bring social change. A Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awardee, she has served as a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha. She has worked extensively on housing rights, women’s empowerment, rural development, and education for the girl child through organisations she leads and supports. Internationally, she is recognised for her advocacy and humanitarian work.
